rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE USE OF THE LEGAL ASSISTANCE FUND AND THE AGARANG  KALINGA AT SAKLOLO PARA SA MGA OFWS NA NANGANGAILANGAN (AKSYON) FUND, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 26 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8042, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "MIGRANT WORKERS AND OVERSEAS FILIPINOS ACT OF 1995," AS AMENDED, AND SECTION 14 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11641, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “DEPARTMENT OF MIGRANT WORKERS ACT”
rows.title_short: Migrant Workers And Overseas Filipinos Act Of 1995
rows.abstract:
Seeks to widen the scope of use of the Legal Assistance Fund from the time of the commencement of the investigation, detention, arrest or indictment all the way to the trial proper up to all levels of appeal a distressed overseas Filipino can avail.
States that the rules on the utilization of the Legal Assistance Fund shall apply similarly to the Agarang Kalinga at Saklolo Para sa mga OFWs na Nangangailangan (AKSYON) Fund.
Mandates the Department of Foreign Affairs to extend legal and other forms of assistance to OFWs in countries and territories where there are no Migrant Workers Offices yet.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2023-11-29, transmitted to the Senate on 2023-12-06 and received by the Senate on 2023-12-06

rows.abstract:
Seeks to reorganize and institutionalize NEDA as a Department to serve as lead integrator of the country´s economic development programs and policies.
Proposes for an Economy and Planning Council responsible for directing and providing overall policy direction on economic issues, and shall act as primary advisory bodies and principal coordinating mechanism to ensure that policy environment is conducive to inclusive and sustainable economic growth.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REINSTITUTING ABSOLUTE DIVORCE AS AN ALTERNATIVE MODE FOR THE DISSOLUTION OF MARRIAGE
rows.title_short: Absolute Divorce Act
rows.abstract: Provides key provisions regarding the following: Grounds upon which a petition for absolute divorce may be filed (legal separation Art.55 of the Family Code, as modified; separation of the spouses in fact for at least five (5) years . . . , and reconciliation is highly improbable; Psychological incapacity; Irreconcilable differences; Domestic or marital abuse to include act under VAWC); dissolution by the proper matrimonial tribunal . . .; Summary Judicial Proceedings; expeditious and affordable court proceedings; Overseas Filipino petitioner´s priority of hearing; 60-day cooling-off period; care and custody of minor children and those under seven (7) years of age; protection of the spouses´ respective legitime, termination and liquidation of the conjugal partnership of gains or the absolute community, and alimony. . .; presumptive legitime to the common children; appointment of a competent third party administrator for absolute community or conjugal partnership property; conversion of pending petitions”¦ into absolute divorce without paying filing fees; pre-nuptial, reconciliatory phase or cooling-off counseling, and postnuptial programs and activities; assistance to victims of abuse through a community-based women´s desk; DSWD with DOJ, PCW, the NYC as implementors.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2024-05-22, transmitted to the Senate on 2024-06-11 and received by the Senate on 2024-06-11
rows.remarks: Withdrawal of co-authorship of Rep.ROMUALDO, Jesus Jurdin M. per letter dated May 21, 2024, received on even date.

rows.title_full: AN ACT RECOGNIZING THE CIVIL EFFECTS OF CANONICAL OR CHURCH DISSOLUTION, OR DECLARATION OF NULLITY OF MARRIAGE
rows.title_short: Recognizing The Civil Effects Of Canonical Or Church Dissolution, Or Declaration Of Nullity Of Marriage
rows.abstract:
Aims to recognize the validity and civil effects of marriages enjoined by the law of the Roman Catholic Church including all other established churches and duly recognized religious denominations.
Proposes key provisions related to the following:  
the same effects as a decree of divorce, annulment, or dissolution of marriage ruled by a competent Philippine Court; determination of the status of children of said marriages; partition on the properties of the spouses; custody of the common children; and the delivery of presumptive legitime. . .

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMICS AND DEVELOPMENT PLANNING, DEFINING ITS FUNCTIONS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Seeks to institutionalize NEDA into a Department of Economics Development Authority (DEDP) and include Mindanao Development Authority (MinDA) as a member of the Council or NEDA Board.
Seeks to push for the inclusion and funding of Mindanao priorities in the national planning and budgeting that shall improve the island-region´s productivity and enable it to contribute further to the country´s growth and development.
Proposes several offices of the DEDP as follows: 
Macroeconomics; Trade, services, and industry; Agriculture, natural resources, and environment; Governance; Social development; Strategic foresight and futures; Innovation; Public investment; Social infrastructure; Connectivity infrastructure;  etc.

rows.author: I051;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING REFORMS IN LAND ADMINISTRATION
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address the below par performance of government agencies undertaking land administration functions such as land surveys, mapping, classification, titling, disposition, and registration.
Proposes to consolidate and streamline within a single agency - land administration powers and functions that are dispersed across the DOJ´s Land Registration Authority and Registries of Deeds and the DENR´s Lands Management Bureau, Land Management Services in the regional, provincial, and community offices, NAMRIA, and CARP Secretariat and its field offices.
Proposes to create the Land Administration Authority (LAA) with powers and functions related to:  functions of geodetic and geophysical surveys, land classification surveys, mapping, aerial photography, remote sensing, management of resource information, and research development thereof; specific limits of forest lands and national parks; all alienable and disposable lands of the public domain and other lands, including foreshore and marsh lands; the remaining Friar Lands; lands of patrimonial property of the NG . . .; original titles to land issued . . . and subsequent dealings of registered lands under Land Registration Act and Property Registration Decree; all types of land surveys including surveys per CA No.141, CARL, IPRA and UDHA.

rows.abstract: Defines “Road Rage” as the aggressive, hostile, or violent behavior in traffic or on the road by a motorist that may include the following: wild gesturing at the other concerned party or any of his/her passengers; cursing or using foul language or any form of verbal insults; any physical attack at another or an attempt thereof, reckless driving; any form of threat or intimidation; any use of force against another person/s; and other analogous circumstances, . . .

rows.author: K089;K102;K140;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE COMMUNITY-DRIVEN DEVELOPMENT (CDD) APPROACH AS A NATIONAL STRATEGY FOR INCLUSIVE GROWTH AND SOCIAL PROTECTION, ESTABLISHING FOR THE PURPOSE THE CDD KNOWLEDGE AND RESOURCE INSTITUTE, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Defines several terms among others - Basic sectors refer to the disadvantaged sectors of Philippine society, including farmer-peasants, fisherfolk, workers in the formal sector including migrant workers, workers in the informal sector, indigenous peoples and cultural communities, women, persons with disability, senior citizens, victims of calamities and disasters, youth and students, children, urban poor, and members Of cooperatives.
Refers Community Driven Development (CDD) as an approach that gives control over the development processes, decision-making, and resources to community members or groups and treats people as assets and partners in the development process while building on their institutions and resources.
Seeks to enact programs that provide opportunities for the poor, vulnerable, and marginalized to participate in the designing, planning, budgeting, implementing, monitoring, and evaluating community programs, activities, and projects. 
Provides capacity-building opportunities for LGUs, civil society organizations (CSOs), and communities to ensure the proper use of the CDD approach in implementing local programs, projects, and activities.
rows.status: Substituted by HB11450

rows.title_full: AN ACT UPGRADING AND CREATING ADDITIONAL POSITIONS IN THE OFFICE OF THE GOVERNMENT CORPORATE COUNSEL (OGCC), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE EXECUTIVE ORDER NO 878 DATED MARCH 4, 1983, AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 299 DATED JULY 26, 1987
rows.abstract:
Proposes to augment the OGCC's workforce to sufficiently address the developing requirements and legal concerns of government corporate sector.
Seeks to maintain OGCC´s effectiveness in addressing the legal needs of its clients particularly corporations which do not have internal legal departments. 
Proposes to strengthen the applicable laws and issuances of OGCC´s organizational structure to create new positions in its hierarchy and augment its present complement with an additional thirty-six (36) lawyer positions.
rows.status: Substituted by HB11039

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL POLICY FOR THE DEVELOPMENT, UTILIZATION, AND COMMERCIALIZATION OF ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEMS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address the country´s continuing dependence on fossil fuels despite the enactment of R.A. No. 9513 or the “Renewable Energy Act of 2008”.
Seeks to establish general incentives to foster development, utilization, and commercialization of ESS in both on-grid and off-grid areas; to streamline licensing and permitting processes needed for the operation of ESS, aligned with the Energy Virtual One-Stop Shop (EVOSS) Act, etc.
Defines several terms among  several others:  
“Energy Storage System” or “ESS” refers to a facility capable of absorbing energy directly from the Grid or distribution system, or from an RE Plant connected to the Grid or Distribution System and storing it for a time period, and injecting stored energy when prompted, needed to ensure reliability and balanced power system.
Provides that ESS shall manage the variability of renewable energy sources and help the country´s electric power sector.
rows.status: Substituted by HB11353

rows.author: E046;
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE BARANGAY AFFAIRS AND DEVELOPMENT COMMISSION, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, ESTABLISHING THE BARANGAY DEVELOPMENT FUND, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Seeks to reexamine the functions of the barangay not only as a political unit but also as an enabler of the community´s socioeconomic affairs.
Seeks to equip barangays with necessary skills to manage their limited resources effectively, generate economic gains, and provide primary local services to their constituents.
Proposes a Barangay Development Fund that will be utilized exclusively for the development projects and programs of the barangays, including subsidies to poor barangays for the honoraria of barangay officials and employees.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2023-11-07
